extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / natural philosophers and experimental scientists (17th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples for conducting, recording, and interpreting natural-history experiments and observations (e.g., insect generation, magnetical variation, anatomical dissections, mining descriptions). Emphasizes experimental controls, precise measurement, documentation, and response to objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controlled coverings to separate air access from insect access
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover vessels with a very fine Naples veil so that air can enter but flies cannot; compare exactly closed vessels, veiled vessels, and open vessels to determine whether worms/flies arise without fly access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Redi's experiment where meat in vessels covered with fine veil received air but produced no worms while open meat was 'fly-blown' and produced larvae. Anti-pattern: attributing vermin generation to putrefaction without preventing insect access. Scoring note: a valid control specifically isolates the suspected causal agent (fly access) while preserving other conditions (air).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fully sealed vessels as negative control
rubrics_metrics.description: When vessels are exactly closed, no insect breeds in them; use completely sealed vessels to test whether generation happens without external agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redi observed that 'in vessels exactly closed, no insect breeds.' Objection to this control (lack of air) must be addressed by complementary controls (e.g., veils). Anti-pattern: treating a sealed-vessel negative result as proof without considering confounding factor of air exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments to refute alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and experimentally address likely objections (for example, that lack of insects in sealed vessels is due to absence of air rather than absence of flies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redi counters the 'want of air' objection by using veiled vessels that admit air but exclude flies. Good practice: design parallel conditions that isolate competing hypotheses. Scoring: stronger when objection-handling controls are explicit and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close, repeated, and careful observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Take 'extraordinary care and pains to observe' — record repeated observations (e.g., flies sitting on flesh before vermination) and document temporal sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redi's conclusions rest on repeated observations that flies were present before larvae appeared. Anti-pattern: single casual observations or reliance on hearsay. Scoring: higher weight to conclusions supported by systematic, repeated observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic verification of life stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use microscopy to examine eggs/nits and distinguish pregnant nits from emptied ones (e.g., lice nits observed under microscope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redi 'having discerned by a microscope some nits yet pregnant with young ones'—microscopic evidence strengthens causal claims about development. Include images/figures where possible. Anti-pattern: claiming egg-stage without observational proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate consistency and determinateness in natural occurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: Document repeating, determinate patterns in nature (e.g., galls always growing on a particular part of a branch; each gall type associated with a peculiar insect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated mapping of occurrences to show non-randomness: 'both the generation of worms in vegetables is always and constantly the same' and 'each sort of galls has its peculiar and determinate race of worms'. Anti-pattern: attributing random causation when patterns are consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider environmental/seasonal effects on biological phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for variation due to season and temperature (e.g., the same flies may be viviparous in some seasons and oviparous in others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redi notes variation 'according to the more or less heat of the season.' Good reports explicitly record environmental conditions and consider them in interpretation. Anti-pattern: ignoring seasonality as a source of variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide anatomical description supported by figures and dissections
rubrics_metrics.description: When making anatomical claims, provide dissection detail and illustrative figures (e.g., muscle structure, muscles' fibre motions, and odd births), and explain methods and observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willis and Grandi include anatomical experiments, figures, and detailed descriptions of odd births and muscle motion. Good reports include illustrations, procedures, and explanations of how dissections support claims. Scoring: higher when specimens, drawings, and stepwise descriptions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address prior literature and explicitly respond to objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with alternative theories and previously published objections, and provide arguments and experiments to vindicate your position (e.g., Willis replying to Dr. Highmore).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willis 'vindicates his doctrine...and proceeds to remove the difficulties and objections'—good work situates itself in dialogue with contemporaries and defends its claims. Anti-pattern: ignoring conflicting published claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise meridian lines and rigorous measurement for magnetic studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish exact meridians and use carefully constructed measurement lines and instruments (e.g., needles of known length) to measure magnetic declination accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auzout's Roman observations were made 'on many meridian lines drawn as exactly as possibly he could with a needle, three quarters of a palm long.' The Royal Society orders that precise meridians be made for observing declination. Guidance: construct reproducible baselines, report instrument dimensions, and note possible local iron interference. Anti-pattern: crude bearings or undocumented baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote systematic, regular, and geographically distributed observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect long-term (yearly) and geographically distributed data to determine trends (e.g., whether declination changes uniformly across Europe and America).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auzout and the editor urge yearly observations at many sites so 'we should already know the progress thereof.' Good practice: coordinate repeat measurements across sites and time. Scoring: stronger evidence when temporal and geographic replication exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and apply established accurate methods; cite method sources
rubrics_metrics.description: When employing specialized measurement methods, cite prior descriptions (e.g., 'he will find several ways of doing it accurately ... in N° 24 of these Tracts') and follow standard procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references to standard protocols so others can reproduce results. Anti-pattern: inventing unreferenced procedures without validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specimens and physical samples for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Send physical specimens (e.g., salt samples, cinnabar, ores) and describe their appearance and how they were collected so others can examine and verify claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Brown 'present[s] you with those two kinds of Transylvanian stone salts' and other specimens; good practice includes sending samples and describing them (colour, crystal form, how broken). Scoring: reproducibility and verifiability increase with available specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe practical procedures in full for reproducibility (mining/metallurgy examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting technical processes (e.g., ore washing, amalgamation with quicksilver, use of pumps and wheels in mines), give step-by-step descriptions, materials used, and local practices so processes can be replicated or assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed steps in ore processing (pounding, washing, kneading with quicksilver, distillation per descensum, engine particulars) are provided as models. Anti-pattern: high-level claims about yields or processes without procedural detail.
